verdicts.note: Compass was described as drawing a circle through a chosen point only, but the later constructions copy radii (equal circles, stepping around a circle). Now says the radius can be a distance already on the page.
The parallel-through-a-point tip said 'draw a second perpendicular' without saying through which point or why that gives a parallel. Clarified.
The square/rhombus sentence is about equal sides, not equal angles, and read as part of the angles argument. Reframed as a separate aside.
'Can add to anything' was loose; reworded to 'need not add to 180 degrees'.

The cube-into-three-pyramids argument only covered base area s^2 and height s, yet claimed the formula for every B and h. Added the box stretch so every height is covered before Cavalieri extends it to every base.
